{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLV1QfJiGuCd7kRrd9gp","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011tgmkQJnAaCVavoAGzAWeM","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-001/2026-07-24T072502Z-claude-no-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# The Approve button: two tickets, one root cause\n\nBoth tickets come from the same wrong assumption baked into this code:\nthat `await writeContractAsync(...)` means \"the approval is done.\" It does\nnot. In wagmi v2, `writeContractAsync` **resolves the moment the wallet\nsigns and broadcasts the transaction and hands back a tx hash** — not when\nthe transaction is mined, and definitely not when the allowance on-chain\nhas changed. On mainnet that leaves a ~12s+ blind spot where the code\nthinks it's finished but nothing on-chain has happened yet.\n\nTwo facts about the current code:\n\n- `writeContractAsync` **resolves at broadcast** (returns the hash), well\n  before confirmation.\n- `isPending` from `useWriteContract` is true **only during the wallet\n  request**. It flips back to false as soon as the promise settles\n  (resolve *or* reject).\n- `useReadContract` with **default options does not watch/poll**. It won't\n  automatically re-read the allowance when a new block lands; it refetches\n  on mount / query-key change / window refocus. So even the \"swap Approve →\n  Stake\" is delayed and depends on luck.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approval transactions\n\n### Why\nThe button's disabled guard is `isPending || submitting`. Both go false the\ninstant `writeContractAsync` **resolves at broadcast** — long before the\napprove tx is mined and long before the allowance read reflects it. During\nthat gap the button is fully live and still reads \"Approve\" (allowance\nstill shows insufficient). The user clicks again and signs a second,\nidentical approval.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | On-chain / wallet | `isPending` | `submitting` | Button |\n|------|-------------------|-------------|--------------|--------|\n| T+0.0s | user clicks; wallet opens | true | true | disabled — \"Approving...\" |\n| T+2s | user confirms; tx **broadcast to mempool**, hash returned; promise resolves; `setSubmitting(false)` runs | false | false | **enabled — \"Approve\"** |\n| T+2s → ~T+14s | approve tx still pending in mempool; allowance unchanged on-chain; `useReadContract` still shows insufficient | false | false | **enabled — \"Approve\"** ← danger window |\n| within that window | **user clicks again** → second approve signed & broadcast | (true briefly) | (true briefly) | second tx sent |\n| ~T+14s (next block) | first approve mines; default `useReadContract` does **not** auto-refetch | false | false | often still \"Approve\" |\n| ~T+26s (block after) | second approve mines | | | two approvals now in wallet activity |\n\nThe 12s block time is what turns a race into a reproducible bug: the\nbutton is guaranteed to sit enabled-and-labeled-\"Approve\" for at least one\nfull block (usually more), which is plenty of time for a real user to\nconclude \"nothing happened\" and click again.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejected approval, button stays dead until reload\n\n### Why\n```js\nonClick={async () => {\n  setSubmitting(true);\n  await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);  // ← throws on user rejection\n  setSubmitting(false);                   // ← never runs\n}}\n```\nWhen the user rejects in the wallet, `writeContractAsync` **rejects**\n(throws `UserRejectedRequestError`). There is no `try/catch/finally`, so\nexecution leaves the handler at the `await` and `setSubmitting(false)`\nnever runs. `submitting` is stuck `true` forever. `isPending` resets to\nfalse on its own, but `disabled={isPending || submitting}` stays true\nbecause of the stuck `submitting`. Only a page reload resets React state.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet)\n\n| Time | Wallet | `isPending` | `submitting` | Button |\n|------|--------|-------------|--------------|--------|\n| T+0.0s | click; `setSubmitting(true)`; wallet opens | true | true | disabled — \"Approving...\" |\n| T+2s | user **rejects** → promise rejects → handler throws before `setSubmitting(false)` | false | **true (stuck)** | disabled — \"Approve\" |\n| forever | — | false | **true (stuck)** | **permanently disabled** |\n| page reload | React state reset | false | false | enabled — \"Approve\" |\n\n---\n\n## The fix: model the states the flow actually has\n\nTwo independent defects, two fixes:\n\n1. **Always release the busy flag** — use `try/finally` so rejection (or any\n   throw) still re-enables the button.\n2. **Stay busy through confirmation, not just broadcast** — the button must\n   remain disabled from click until the approval is *mined* and the\n   *allowance re-read reflects it*. Use `useWaitForTransactionReceipt` on\n   the returned hash, then invalidate/refetch the allowance. Never re-enable\n   on broadcast alone.\n\n```jsx\nconst { writeContractAsync } = useWriteContract();\nconst [approveHash, setApproveHash] = useState(undefined);\nconst [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n// allowance read — give it a stable queryKey so we can refetch it\nconst { data: allowance, refetch: refetchAllowance } = useReadContract(allowanceArgs);\n\n// wait for the approve tx to actually mine\nconst { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess: isConfirmed } =\n  useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash: approveHash });\n\n// once mined, pull the fresh allowance so the UI can swap to Stake\nuseEffect(() => {\n  if (isConfirmed) refetchAllowance();\n}, [isConfirmed, refetchAllowance]);\n\n// busy spans the whole flow: signing → mempool → mined → allowance refetched\nconst busy = submitting || isConfirming;\n\n<button\n  disabled={busy}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      const hash = await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);\n      setApproveHash(hash);          // hand off to receipt watcher\n    } catch (err) {\n      // user rejected or tx failed — surface a toast/message here\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);          // ALWAYS runs → fixes Ticket 2\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {busy ? \"Approving...\" : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\nWhy this fixes each ticket:\n\n- **Ticket 1:** After broadcast, `submitting` goes false but\n  `approveHash` is set, so `isConfirming` is true → `busy` stays true and\n  the button stays disabled through the full 12s+ block window. When the\n  receipt lands, `refetchAllowance()` updates the allowance, and the UI\n  swaps Approve → Stake. There is no enabled-\"Approve\" gap to double-click.\n- **Ticket 2:** The `finally` block runs on rejection, so `submitting`\n  returns to false; `approveHash` was never set, so `isConfirming` is false\n  → `busy` is false → the button is live and clickable again immediately,\n  no reload needed.\n\n### Notes / gotchas\n- The core bug is treating a broadcast as a completion. The single\n  discipline that prevents both tickets: **the button is busy from click\n  until the receipt is mined and the allowance re-read reflects it — not\n  from click until the hash comes back.**\n- Don't rely on default `useReadContract` to notice the new allowance on\n  its own; drive the refetch off the receipt (as above) or invalidate the\n  allowance query key. Otherwise the button can linger on \"Approve\" even\n  after a successful approval.\n- Distinguish user-rejection from real tx failure in the `catch` (e.g.\n  check for `UserRejectedRequestError`) so you only show an error toast for\n  genuine failures.\n```\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5882,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5882},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0dc2e2e2-9fe6-43c7-bcba-9f2fe09f84a0","uuid":"05709cbf-ab12-4f9f-9c92-ff484ed795ac","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:26:21.208Z","request_id":"req_011CdLV1N9zZkjvHe1p9UmDz"}

On mainnet that leaves a ~12s+ blind spot where the code\nthinks it's finished but nothing on-chain has happened yet.\n\nTwo facts about the current code:\n\n- `writeContractAsync` **resolves at broadcast** (returns the hash), well\n  before confirmation.\n- `isPending` from `useWriteContract` is true **only during the wallet\n  request**. It flips back to false as soon as the promise settles\n  (resolve *or* reject).\n- `useReadContract` with **default options does not watch/poll**. It won't\n  automatically re-read the allowance when a new block lands; it refetches\n  on mount / query-key change / window refocus. So even the \"swap Approve →\n  Stake\" is delayed and depends on luck.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approval transactions\n\n### Why\nThe button's disabled guard is `isPending || submitting`. Both go false the\ninstant `writeContractAsync` **resolves at broadcast** — long before the\napprove tx is mined and long before the allowance read reflects it. During\nthat gap the button is fully live and still reads \"Approve\" (allowance\nstill shows insufficient). The user clicks again and signs a second,\nidentical approval.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | On-chain / wallet | `isPending` | `submitting` | Button |\n|------|-------------------|-------------|--------------|--------|\n| T+0.0s | user clicks; wallet opens | true | true | disabled — \"Approving...\" |\n| T+2s | user confirms; tx **broadcast to mempool**, hash returned; promise resolves; `setSubmitting(false)` runs | false | false | **enabled — \"Approve\"** |\n| T+2s → ~T+14s | approve tx still pending in mempool; allowance unchanged on-chain; `useReadContract` still shows insufficient | false | false | **enabled — \"Approve\"** ← danger window |\n| within that window | **user clicks again** → second approve signed & broadcast | (true briefly) | (true briefly) | second tx sent |\n| ~T+14s (next block) | first approve mines; default `useReadContract` does **not** auto-refetch | false | false | often still \"Approve\" |\n| ~T+26s (block after) | second approve mines | | | two approvals now in wallet activity |\n\nThe 12s block time is what turns a race into a reproducible bug: the\nbutton is guaranteed to sit enabled-and-labeled-\"Approve\" for at least one\nfull block (usually more), which is plenty of time for a real user to\nconclude \"nothing happened\" and click again.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejected approval, button stays dead until reload\n\n### Why\n```js\nonClick={async () => {\n  setSubmitting(true);\n  await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);  // ← throws on user rejection\n  setSubmitting(false);                   // ← never runs\n}}\n```\nWhen the user rejects in the wallet, `writeContractAsync` **rejects**\n(throws `UserRejectedRequestError`). There is no `try/catch/finally`, so\nexecution leaves the handler at the `await` and `setSubmitting(false)`\nnever runs. `submitting` is stuck `true` forever. `isPending` resets to\nfalse on its own, but `disabled={isPending || submitting}` stays true\nbecause of the stuck `submitting`. Only a page reload resets React state.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet)\n\n| Time | Wallet | `isPending` | `submitting` | Button |\n|------|--------|-------------|--------------|--------|\n| T+0.0s | click; `setSubmitting(true)`; wallet opens | true | true | disabled — \"Approving...\" |\n| T+2s | user **rejects** → promise rejects → handler throws before `setSubmitting(false)` | false | **true (stuck)** | disabled — \"Approve\" |\n| forever | — | false | **true (stuck)** | **permanently disabled** |\n| page reload | React state reset | false | false | enabled — \"Approve\" |\n\n---\n\n## The fix: model the states the flow actually has\n\nTwo independent defects, two fixes:\n\n1. **Always release the busy flag** — use `try/finally` so rejection (or any\n   throw) still re-enables the button.\n2. **Stay busy through confirmation, not just broadcast** — the button must\n   remain disabled from click until the approval is *mined* and the\n   *allowance re-read reflects it*. Use `useWaitForTransactionReceipt` on\n   the returned hash, then invalidate/refetch the allowance. Never re-enable\n   on broadcast alone.\n\n```jsx\nconst { writeContractAsync } = useWriteContract();\nconst [approveHash, setApproveHash] = useState(undefined);\nconst [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n// allowance read — give it a stable queryKey so we can refetch it\nconst { data: allowance, refetch: refetchAllowance } = useReadContract(allowanceArgs);\n\n// wait for the approve tx to actually mine\nconst { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess: isConfirmed } =\n  useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash: approveHash });\n\n// once mined, pull the fresh allowance so the UI can swap to Stake\nuseEffect(() => {\n  if (isConfirmed) refetchAllowance();\n}, [isConfirmed, refetchAllowance]);\n\n// busy spans the whole flow: signing → mempool → mined → allowance refetched\nconst busy = submitting || isConfirming;\n\n<button\n  disabled={busy}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      const hash = await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);\n      setApproveHash(hash);          // hand off to receipt watcher\n    } catch (err) {\n      // user rejected or tx failed — surface a toast/message here\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);          // ALWAYS runs → fixes Ticket 2\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {busy ? \"Approving...\" : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\nWhy this fixes each ticket:\n\n- **Ticket 1:** After broadcast, `submitting` goes false but\n  `approveHash` is set, so `isConfirming` is true → `busy` stays true and\n  the button stays disabled through the full 12s+ block window.
